title.narrative: South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation Power Transmission and Distribution System Strengthening Project

description.narrative: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) will provide a loan to the Government of Nepal (the government) to (a) upgrade 220/132 kilovolt (kV) substations to 400/220/132 kV substations to enable electricity generated from independent power producer (IPPs) plants in the Khimti hydropower corridor to be exported to India; (b) construction of three 132/11 kV substations in Teku, Koteshwor, and Thapathali which will increase supply capacity into the Kathmandu Valley; (c) modernizing and reinforcing four distribution centers around Kathmandu Valley to be able to meet increasing domestic demand for electricity; and (d) construction of 33 kV, 11 kV, and 0.4 kV lines and substations to facilitate connection of approximately 150,000 new customers in Nepal's Province 2 in the country's southeast region The proposed project complements the efforts of Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) to strengthen parts of Nepal's high-voltage transmission network and complete Nepal's portion of the second cross-border transmission line with India for increasing electricity trade.

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Distribution system in the Kathmandu Valley, Bharatpur, and Pokhara, and consumers awareness on energy efficiency and safety improved. Indicator: 10 new 33/11 kV substations, 350 circuit-km of 33 kV lines, 1,000 circuit-km of 11 kV lines, and 960 circuit-km of low-voltage lines commissioned in Province 2 (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: The contract was divided into 5 lots and all were awarded to M/s Tata Projects Limited, India.
Lot 1: 99% of substation work but only 65% work completed on 33Kv transmission lines. physical progress. Work has been delayed due to supply of transmission line materials by the contractor.
Lot-2: As of 30 June 2026, the physical progress is 83%. Work affected due to delay in supply of materials by contractor and ROW issues.
Lot-3: Physical progress of 80%. Work affected due to delay in supply of materials.
Lot-4: 62% physical progress. Work affected due to ROW challenges and delay in material supply.
Lot-5: Overall physical progress of 50%. Work progress is very slow than expected, due to ROW issue and public obstruction in different areas like Kalaiya SS to Matiarwa chowk, Bisharampur road Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 1 new 132/66/11 kV automated substation in Koteshwor commissioned (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: IFB published on 12 June 2026 with the bid submission date extended till 17 August 2026. Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 1,265 MVA of 400/220 kV transformer capacity installed in three substations in New Khimti, Barhabise, and Lapsiphedi (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Pakage A2 (Upgrading substations at Khimti, Barabishe, and Lapshiphedi):
Progress as of 30 June 2026 are:
Khimti S/S: 97% physical progress. Erection and testing completed. Energization pending due to NEA's bypass arrangement.
Barhaise S/S: 92% physical progress. Electrical and civil works are in closing stage. Pre-commissioning testing completed.
Lapsiphedi S/s: 81% physical progress and completion expected by December 2026, provided there are no public obstructions Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 12 km 132 kV double-circuit transmission line from Bhaktapur to Koteshwor, and 2 km 66 kV transmission line from Koteshwor to Banewsor commissioned (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Package A1.1: IFB published on 29 June 2026.
Package A1.2- Construction of 132 kV line from Bhaktapur substation to Thimi substation and bay addition works at Bhaktapur substation: The package includes 132 kV double circuit underground line from Thimi Substation to Balkumari Substation, and 66 kV LILO of existing Baneshwor-Bhaktapur-Patan line. The contract for this package was awarded to KEC International Limited of India on 14 December 2022.
Overall 80% physical progress achieved as of end June 2026. For remaining work areas, work clearance pending from NEA, particularly coordination with DOR for road cutting permit Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 9 distribution centers in the Kathmandu Valley, the Bharatpur distribution center in Chitwan district, and the Pokhara distribution center in Kaski district reinforced and modernized (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Two packages awarded: (i) distribution system reinforcement and modernization of Easter-western part of Kathmandu Valley - package awarded to the M/S Larsen & Toubro Limited, India, on 24 June 2020 with a contract closing date of 19 December 2023. Survey, design, and first lots of materials completed.
The overall physical progress is 70%. Work has been delayed due to road cutting permit/footpath and right of way challenges.

Contract was awarded to M/s TATA Projects Limited, India on 24 June 2021. Overall physical progress as of end June 2026 is 65%. Progress affected due to delay in supply of materials, road cutting permits and ROW challenges. Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:
